nodes.statement: Suppose there are k occupations (e.g., hunting, fishing, and woodcutting) and, for each occupation i, the expected income for workers with feature vector x is given by y_i(x)=x^top w_i^star + xi_i, where w_i^star is a parameter vector and xi_i sim normal01 captures the sum of independent market events related to the i-th occupation. nodes.name: Max Self-Selection \cite{cherapanamjeri2023selfselection}
nodes.statement: In linear regression with self-selection bias under the maximum selection criterion, a sample (x,y_max) in R^d times R is generated as follows: item A covariate x is drawn from normal0I, and item y_max is the maximum of k different unknown linear functions of x that are independently perturbed by noise, i.e., y_max = max_i in [k] setx^top w_i^star + xi_i, where w_1^star,dots,w_k^star are the unknown target parameters and xi_1,dots,xi_k are independent normal01 random variables. The unknown parameters w_1^star,dots,w_k^star satisfy the following conditions: item[(a)] (Separability)~~ relaxw^star_i_2^2 geq Omega(1) + max_jneq i~sabssinanglew^star_j, w^star_i. item[(b)] (Boundedness) ~~max_1leq ileq krelaxw^star_i_2leq O(1)\,.

nodes.name: \textbf{Information Preservation}
nodes.statement: Given constants alphain [0,1], true parameters (mu^star,Sigma^star) of a d-dimensional Gaussian distribution normalmu^starSigma^star, and a partition hypoP of the domain R^d, hypoP is said to be alpha-information preserving at radius R>0 with respect to normalmu^starSigma^star if, for any parameters (mu,Sigma) that are R-close to (mu^star,Sigma^star) in ell_2-norm,footnote For a matrix A, relaxA_F denotes its Frobenious norm and is defined as relaxA_F^2=sum_isum_j A_ij^2. it holds that \[ tv coarseNormalmuSigmahypoP coarseNormalmu^starSigma^starhypoP geq mininbrace 1, alpha inparen relaxmu - mu^star_2^2 + relaxSigma - Sigma^star_F^2 ^1/2 \,.footnote Taking a minimum on the RHS is somewhat redundant since the TV distance is upper bounded by 1. However, this serves as a useful notational reminder of this restriction when carrying out calculations. \]

nodes.statement: Note that information preservation is defined with respect to the true parameters (mu^star,Sigma^star), and it can vary significantly with different true parameters. Moreover, the radius parameter \(R\) imposes a local structure by allowing information to be preserved only in a ball of radius \(R\) around the true parameters. This locality is essential; for example, in problems with permutation invariance on the true parameters (e.g., the self-selection problem of Crefdef:ssb or mixture models), as any permutation of the true parameters would make the LHS of Crefdef:informationPreservation zero, but the RHS would be positive.

nodes.raw_latex:
Consider the Gaussian distribution $\normal{\mu^\star}{I}$, with mean $\mu^\star \in \mathbb{R}^d$ and identity covariance matrix.
Consider a distribution $\uppi$ over partitions of $\mathbb{R}^d$.
We generate a sample as follows:
\begin{enumerate}[itemsep=1pt]
    \item Draw $z$ from $\normal{\mu^\star}{I}$ and, independently, draw a partition $\hypo{P}$ of $\mathbb{R}^d$ from $\uppi$.
    \item Observe the unique set $P \in \hypo{P}$ that contains $z$.
\end{enumerate}
We denote the distribution of $S$ as $\customcal{N}_\uppi(\mu^\star, I)$.

\label{thm:SS}
            Suppose \cref{asmp:SS:gaussianity,asmp:SS:separationBoundedness} hold.

                given any $\varepsilon,\delta\in (0,1)$ 
                and

            The algorithm runs in time \mbox{$\mathrm{poly}(d,k,\nfrac{1}{\varepsilon},{\log(\nicefrac1\delta)}) + {2^{\wt{O}(k)}}$}.

nodes.raw_latex:
\label{thm:SS:localConvexity}
            Suppose \cref{asmp:SS:gaussianity,asmp:SS:separationBoundedness} hold with constants $c,C>0$.
            Fix a permutation $w_1^\star,w_2^\star,\dots,w_k^\star$ of the vectors $\inbrace{w_i^\star:1\leq i\leq k}$.
            The following hold. 
            \begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=15pt]
                \item \textit{(Information Preservation)}
                    For any matrices $V,W\in \mathbb{R}^{d\times k}$ that are $O\inparen{\nfrac{1}{\log{k}}}$-warm starts for ${W^\star}$, 
                    \[
                        \tv{\customcal{M}(V)}{~\customcal{M}(W)} \geq 
                        \inparen{\frac{c}{ek}}^{{O({C^2/c^2}){}}}
                        \cdot \relax{V - W}_F\,.
                        \addtocounter{equation}{1}\tag{\theequation}\label{eq:SS:informationPreservation}
                    \]
                \item \textit{(Local Convexity)} For any matrix $W\in \mathbb{R}^{d\times k}$ that is a $\mathrm{poly}\inparen{\nfrac{1}{k}}$-warm start for ${W^\star}$, 
                    \[
                        \grad^2 \ensuremath{\mathscr{L}}(W) \succeq 0\,.
                    \]
            \end{enumerate}

                \[
                    \grad^2 \ensuremath{\mathscr{L}}(W) \succeq 0\,.
                \]
        \end{enumerate}

\label{thm:convexPartitionMeanEstimation}
        Let $\varepsilon\in (0, 1]$.
        Suppose $\hypo{P}$ is a convex $\alpha$-information preserving partition of $\mathbb{R}^d$ 
        with respect to $\normal{{\mu^\star}}{I}$
        and $\relax{{\mu^\star}}_2\leq D$.
        There is an algorithm that outputs an estimate $\widetilde \mu$ satisfying
        \[
            \relax{\widetilde \mu - {\mu^\star}}_2 \leq \varepsilon
        \]
        with probability $1-\delta$. Moreover, the algorithm requires
        \[
            m = \widetilde O\inparen{\frac{dD^2\log(\nfrac1\delta)}{\alpha^4} + \frac{d\log(\nfrac1\delta)}{\alpha^4\varepsilon^2}}
        \]
        i.i.d.{} samples from $\coarseNormal{{\mu^\star}}{I}{\hypo{P}}$ and $\mathrm{poly}(m, T_s)$ time,
        where $T_s$ is the time complexity of sampling from a Gaussian distribution truncated to a set $P\in \hypo{P}$.
        {Moreover,
        if the facet-complexity\footnote{The \emph{facet-complexity} \cite[Definition 6.2.2]{grotschel1988geometric} of a polytope is a natural measure of the complexity of the polytope.
        See \Cref{apx:sampling-polytopes:removing-oracle-assumption} for the formal definition and more details.}
        of every observed set $P$ is bounded above by $\varphi$,
        we may assume $T_s = \mathrm{poly}(d, \varphi)$.}

            For a non-empty set $\ensuremath{\mathscr{E}}\subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$,

\label{thm:SS:LC:formal}
    For $\rho\in(0,k^{-\Omega(B^2)})$, $t=\rho\cdot \wt{O}\inparen{\frac{1}{C^2B^4k^{17/2}}}$, and $V\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times k}$ satisfying $\relax{V}_F=1$,

    \[
        W_t\coloneqq W^\star+tV\,.
    \]
    Then, 
    \[
        \boldsymbol\NABLA^2 \ensuremath{\mathscr{L}}(W_t) 
        \succeq 
        \boldsymbol\NABLA^2 \ensuremath{\mathscr{L}}(W^\star)
            - (\rho + k^{-\Omega(B^2)}) I\,.

\label{lem:SS:LC:step1}
For $\zeta\in(0,1)$ and $t=\zeta\cdot O\inparen{\frac{1}{B^4k^3}}$, 
\[
    \forall_{x\in \mathbb{R}^d}\,,~\forall_{y_{\max}\in \mathbb{R}}\,,\quad 
    \boldsymbol\NABLA^2 \ensuremath{\mathscr{L}}(W_t;x,y_{\max}) - \boldsymbol\NABLA^2 \ensuremath{\mathscr{L}}(W_0;x,y_{\max}) \succeq -\upgamma(x,y_{\max}) \cdot I_{k}\otimes xx^\top\,,
\]
where
\[ 
    \upgamma(x,y_{\max}) \coloneqq 
        80 k^2\cdot
        \Bigl(\zeta + e^{-B^2 k/2}\Bigr)\cdot
        \Bigl(1 + y_{\max}^4 + \max\sinbrace{\|W_t^\top x\|_\infty, \|W_0^\top x\|_\infty}^4\Bigr)
        \,.
\]

nodes.statement: Fix V with relaxV_F=1. We will prove the desired statement for rhoin (0,1) but only need the smaller range to establish crefthm:SS:LC:formal. Define \[ t=rhocdot wtOinparenfrac1C^2B^4k^17/2 qquadtextand zeta=rhocdot frac1k^11/2 C^2\,. addtocounterequation1tagtheequation \] By construction, \[ t = zeta cdot wtOinparenfrac1B^4k^3\,. \] Hence, creflem:SS:LC:step1 is applicable with (t,zeta) and implies that, for each x, we have \[ operatornamewithlimitsE_y_maxBigl[boldsymbolNABLA^2 ensuremathL(W_t;x,y_max) - boldsymbolNABLA^2 ensuremathL(W_0;x,y_max)Bigr] succeq -operatornamewithlimitsE_y_maxbigl[upgamma(x,y_max)bigr]\, I_kotimes xx^top\,. \] Averaging over x, we deduce \[ operatornamewithlimitsE_x,y_maxBigl[boldsymbolNABLA^2 ensuremathL(W_t;x,y_max) - boldsymbolNABLA^2 ensuremathL(W_0;x,y_max)Bigr] succeq -operatornamewithlimitsE_x,y_maxBigl[upgamma(x,y_max) cdot I_kotimes xx^topBigr]\,. \] Since boldsymbolNABLA^2 ensuremathL(W)=operatornamewithlimitsE_x,y_max[boldsymbolNABLA^2 ensuremathL(W;x,y_max)] for any W, we obtain \[ boldsymbolNABLA^2 ensuremathL(W_t) - boldsymbolNABLA^2 ensuremathL(W_0) succeq -operatornamewithlimitsE_x,y_maxBigl[upgamma(x,y_max) cdot I_kotimes xx^topBigr]\,. \] Substituting the upper bound on operatornamewithlimitsE_x,y_maxBigl[upgamma(x,y_max) cdot I_kotimes xx^topBigr] from creflem:SS:LC:step2 implies, \[ boldsymbolNABLA^2 ensuremathL(W_t) - boldsymbolNABLA^2 ensuremathL(W_0) succeq -wtO(Ck^11/2)cdot (zeta+e^-B^2k/2)cdot I_dk\,. \] Substituting the value of rho from crefeq:SS:LC:defZetaVal, we deduce that \[ boldsymbolNABLA^2 ensuremathL(W_t) - boldsymbolNABLA^2 ensuremathL(W_0) succeq -(rho+ wtO(Ck^11/2) e^-B^2k/2)cdot I_dk\,. \] Hence, for a suitably large constant in the definition of B (crefeq:SS:LC:defB), we have, \[ boldsymbolNABLA^2 ensuremathL(W_t) - boldsymbolNABLA^2 ensuremathL(W_0) succeq -(rho + e^-Omega(B^2k))cdot I_dk\,. \] This is the required bound since W_0=W^star (by construction).
nodes.raw_latex:
Fix $V$ with $\relax{V}_F=1$.
    We will prove the desired statement for $\rho\in (0,1)$
    but only need the smaller range to establish \cref{thm:SS:LC:formal}.
    Define
    \[
        t=\rho\cdot \wt{O}\inparen{\frac{1}{C^{2}B^{4}k^{17/2}}}
        \qquadtext{and} 
        \zeta=\rho\cdot \frac{1}{k^{11/2} C^{2}}\,.
        \addtocounter{equation}{1}\tag{\theequation}\label{eq:SS:LC:defZetaVal}
    \]
    By construction,
    \[ 
        t = \zeta \cdot \wt{O}\inparen{\frac{1}{B^{4}k^{3}}}\,.
    \]
    Hence, \cref{lem:SS:LC:step1} is applicable with $(t,\zeta)$ and implies that, for each $x$, we have
    \[
    \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}_{y_{\max}}\Bigl[\boldsymbol\NABLA^2 \ensuremath{\mathscr{L}}(W_t;x,y_{\max}) - \boldsymbol\NABLA^2 \ensuremath{\mathscr{L}}(W_0;x,y_{\max})\Bigr] \succeq -\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}_{y_{\max}}\bigl[\upgamma(x,y_{\max})\bigr]\, I_{k}\otimes xx^\top\,.
    \]
Averaging over $x$, we deduce
\[
\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}_{x,y_{\max}}\Bigl[\boldsymbol\NABLA^2 \ensuremath{\mathscr{L}}(W_t;x,y_{\max}) - \boldsymbol\NABLA^2 \ensuremath{\mathscr{L}}(W_0;x,y_{\max})\Bigr] \succeq -\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}_{x,y_{\max}}\Bigl[\upgamma(x,y_{\max}) \cdot I_{k}\otimes xx^\top\Bigr]\,.
\]
Since $\boldsymbol\NABLA^2 \ensuremath{\mathscr{L}}(W)=\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}_{x,y_{\max}}[\boldsymbol\NABLA^2 \ensuremath{\mathscr{L}}(W;x,y_{\max})]$ for any $W$, we obtain
\[
\boldsymbol\NABLA^2 \ensuremath{\mathscr{L}}(W_t) - \boldsymbol\NABLA^2 \ensuremath{\mathscr{L}}(W_0) \succeq -\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}_{x,y_{\max}}\Bigl[\upgamma(x,y_{\max}) \cdot I_{k}\otimes xx^\top\Bigr]\,.
\]
Substituting the upper bound on $\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}_{x,y_{\max}}\Bigl[\upgamma(x,y_{\max}) \cdot I_{k}\otimes xx^\top\Bigr]$ from \cref{lem:SS:LC:step2} implies, 
\[
    \boldsymbol\NABLA^2 \ensuremath{\mathscr{L}}(W_t) - \boldsymbol\NABLA^2 \ensuremath{\mathscr{L}}(W_0) \succeq -\wt{O}(Ck^{11/2})\cdot (\zeta+e^{-B^2k/2})\cdot I_{dk}\,.
\]
Substituting the value of $\rho$ from \cref{eq:SS:LC:defZetaVal}, we deduce that
\[
    \boldsymbol\NABLA^2 \ensuremath{\mathscr{L}}(W_t) - \boldsymbol\NABLA^2 \ensuremath{\mathscr{L}}(W_0) \succeq -(\rho+ \wt{O}(Ck^{11/2}) e^{-B^2k/2})\cdot I_{dk}\,.
\]
Hence, for a suitably large constant in the definition of $B$ (\cref{eq:SS:LC:defB}), we have,
\[
    \boldsymbol\NABLA^2 \ensuremath{\mathscr{L}}(W_t) - \boldsymbol\NABLA^2 \ensuremath{\mathscr{L}}(W_0) \succeq -(\rho + e^{-\Omega(B^2k)})\cdot I_{dk}\,.
\]
This is the required bound since $W_0={W^\star}$ (by construction).

nodes.raw_latex:
The triangle inequality and the fact that $(a+b)^\ell\leq \ell(a^\ell+b^\ell)$ for $a,b\geq 0$ implies
        \[
            \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}_{v}\relax{v}_\infty^\ell 
            \leq 
            \ell \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}_{v}\relax{v-\mu}_\infty^\ell 
            + 
            \ell\relax{\mu}_\infty^\ell\,.
        \]
        Define $M\coloneqq \relax{v-\mu}_\infty$.
        It remains to upper bound $ \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}_{v}[M^\ell]$.
        Observe that,
        \begin{align*}
            \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}[M^\ell] 
            = \int_0^\infty \Pr[M^\ell > w] {\rm d} w 
            = \int_0^\infty \ell r^{\ell-1}\Pr[M > r] {\rm d} r\,.
        \end{align*}
        We divide the integral into two parts:
        \[
            \int_{} \ell r^{\ell-1}\Pr[M > r]{\rm d} r
            = 
                \int_{0}^{2\sqrt{10+\log{k}}} \ell r^{\ell-1}\Pr[M > r]{\rm d} r
                +
                \int_{2\sqrt{10+\log{k}}}^\infty \ell r^{\ell-1}\Pr[M > r]{\rm d} r\,.
                \addtocounter{equation}{1}\tag{\theequation}\label{eq:SS:LC:GaussMaxMoments:twoTermSum}
        \]
        Since $\Pr[M > r]\leq 1$, the first term satisfies the following upper bound 
        \[
            \int_{0}^{2\sqrt{10+\log{k}}} \ell r^{\ell-1}\Pr[M > r]{\rm d} r
            \leq \ell \cdot 2^{\ell} \cdot \inparen{10+\log{k}}^{\ell/2}\,.
        \]
        Next observe that, for any $r\geq 0$,
        \[
            \Pr[M > r]
            \leq k\cdot \Pr_{z\sim \customcal{N}(0,1)}[z>r] 
            \Stackrel{}{\leq}
                \frac{2k}{r}\cdot e^{-r^2/2}\,.
                \addtocounter{equation}{1}\tag{\theequation}\label{eq:SS:LC:tailBound}
        \]
        Where the last inequality uses a standard Gaussian tail bound, see \cref{fact:GaussianTail}.
        Therefore, the second term satisfies the following upper bound
        \[
            \int_{2\sqrt{10+\log{k}}}^\infty \ell r^{\ell-1}\Pr[M > r]{\rm d} r
            ~~\Stackrel{\textup{\tagform@{\ref{eq:SS:LC:tailBound}}}}{\leq }~~
            2k \int_{2\sqrt{10+\log{k}}}^\infty \ell r^{\ell-2} e^{-r^2/2}{\rm d} r\,.
        \]
        Since $\ell\in [0,6]$, $2\sqrt{10+\log{k}}\geq 6$, $\int_{6}^\infty r^{2\ell-4} e^{-r^2/2}{\rm d} r\leq 1$,\footnote{For $z\ge6$ and $0\le x\le6$, we have $z^{2x-4}\le z^8$, so it suffices to show that $\int_{6}^{\infty}z^8e^{-z^2/2}{\rm d} z\leq 1.$
        Substituting $u=z^2/2$, transforms the integral into $2^{7/2}\int_{18}^\infty u^{7/2} e^{-u} {\rm d} u = 2^{7/2}\Gamma(9/2,18)\approx 0.005 \le 1$; where $\Gamma(x,s)\coloneqq \int_{x}^\infty u^{s-1} e^{-u}{\rm d} u$.} and $\int_0^\infty e^{-r^2/2} {\rm d} r\leq 2$,
        the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality implies 
        \begin{align*}
            \int_{2\sqrt{10+\log{k}}}^\infty \ell r^{\ell-2} e^{-r^2/2}{\rm d} r
            \leq 
            \sqrt{\int_{2\sqrt{10+\log{k}}}^\infty \ell^2 r^{2\ell-4} e^{-
            r^2/2}{\rm d} r}
            \cdot 
            \sqrt{\int_{0}^\infty e^{-r^2/2}{\rm d} r}
            \leq 2\ell\,.
        \end{align*}
        Substituting the bounds on the first and second term of \cref{eq:SS:LC:GaussMaxMoments:twoTermSum} into \cref{eq:SS:LC:GaussMaxMoments:twoTermSum} implies,
        \[
            \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}[M^\ell]
            \leq 
            \ell 2^\ell \cdot \inparen{10+\log{k}}^{\ell/2}
            + 2\ell
            ~~~~\Stackrel{(0\leq \ell\leq 6)}{\leq}~~~~
                12 + 384\cdot \inparen{10+\log{k}}^{\ell/2}
            \,.
        \]

nodes.name: Proof of \cref{lem:SS:LC:prob}
nodes.statement: Consider a dtimes k matrix \[ M= m_1 & m_2 & dots & m_k \,. \] Rotate the coordinate system (and re-order if necessary) so that m_1,dots,m_k lie in the span of the first k standard basis vectors e_1,dots,e_k. Since customcalN(0,I) is rotation invariant, xsimnormal0I remains unchanged. Consequently, M^top x depends only on the first k entries of x, i.e., \[ x_1:k=inparenx_1,x_2,dots,x_k\,. \] Since relaxM_2leq relaxM_F, \[ snormM^top x_2 leq relaxM_2relaxx_1:k_2 leq relaxM_Frelaxx_1:k_2\,. \] Standard concentration for the norm of a k-dimensional standard Gaussian shows that, with probability at least 1-(nfracdelta3), \[ relaxx_1:k_2 le sqrtk + Oinparensqrtlognfrac1delta\,. \] Now, set M=W_0 or M=V, and note that by construction relaxV_F=1 and by crefasmp:SS:separationBoundedness each relaxw_i^starle C. Consider a $d\times k$ matrix 
        \[
        M=\begin{bmatrix} m_1 & m_2 & \dots & m_k \end{bmatrix}\,.
        \]
        Rotate the coordinate system (and re-order if necessary) so that $m_1,\dots,m_k$ lie in the span of the first $k$ standard basis vectors $e_1,\dots,e_k$. 
        Since $\customcal{N}(0,I)$ is rotation invariant, $x\sim\normal{0}{I}$ remains unchanged. 
        Consequently, $M^\top x$ depends only on the first $k$ entries of $x$, \emph{i.e.}{}, 
        \[
        x_{1:k}=\inparen{x_1,x_2,\dots,x_k}\,.
        \] 
        Since $\relax{M}_2\leq \relax{M}_F$,
        \[
            \snorm{M^\top x}_2
            \leq  \relax{M}_2\relax{x_{1:k}}_2
            \leq  \relax{M}_F\relax{x_{1:k}}_2\,.
        \]
        Standard concentration for the norm of a $k$-dimensional standard Gaussian shows that, with probability at least $1-(\nfrac{\delta}{3})$,
        \[
        \relax{x_{1:k}}_2 \le \sqrt{k} + O\inparen{\sqrt{\log\nfrac{1}{\delta}}}\,.
        \]
        Now, set $M=W_0$ or $M=V$, and note that by construction $\relax{V}_F=1$ and by \cref{asmp:SS:separationBoundedness} each $\relax{w_i^\star}\le C$. Hence, with probability at least $1-(\nfrac{\delta}{3})$,
        \begin{align*}
            \snorm{V^\top x}_2 \le \sqrt{k} + O\inparen{\sqrt{\log\nfrac{1}{\delta}}}
                \quadtext{and}
            \snorm{W_0^\top x}_2 \le kC\inparen{\sqrt{k} + O\inparen{\sqrt{\log\nfrac{1}{\delta}}}}\,.
        \addtocounter{equation}{1}\tag{\theequation}\label{eq:SS:LC:eventWHP:1}
        \end{align*}
        Since $W_t=W_0+tV$ with $t\le 1$, we obtain
        \[
            \snorm{W_t^\top x}_2 
            ~~\le~~ \snorm{W_0^\top x}_2 + t\,\snorm{V^\top x}_2 
            ~~\Stackrel{(C\geq 1)}{\le}~~ 
                2kC\inparen{\sqrt{k} + O\inparen{\sqrt{\log\nfrac{1}{\delta}}}}\,.
        \addtocounter{equation}{1}\tag{\theequation}\label{eq:SS:LC:eventWHP:2}
        \]
        Moreover, since 
        \[
        z\sim \customcal{N}(W_t^\top x, I_{k})\,,
        \]
        then by Gaussian concentration, with probability at least $1-(\nfrac{\delta}{3})$,
        \[
            \snorm{z-W_t^\top x}_2 \le \sqrt{k} + O\Bigl(\sqrt{\log\nfrac{1}{\delta}}\Bigr)\,.
            \addtocounter{equation}{1}\tag{\theequation}\label{eq:SS:LC:eventWHP:event2}
        \]
        Thus, combining this with \cref{eq:SS:LC:eventWHP:2}, if the events in \cref{eq:SS:LC:eventWHP:1,eq:SS:LC:eventWHP:event2} hold, then, 
        \[
        \relax{z}_2 
            ~~\Stackrel{(C\geq 1)}{\le}~~ 3kC\Bigl(\sqrt{k} + O\Bigl(\sqrt{\log\nfrac{1}{\delta}}\Bigr)\Bigr)\,.
        \]
        Taking a union bound over the events and setting $\delta=e^{-B^2k}$ completes the proof.

Define 
        \[
        \mu_t \coloneqq W_t^\top x\,.
        \]
        Then, for any $y$, 
        \begin{align}
        \frac{\normalMass{\mu_t}{I}{y}}{\normalMass{\mu_0}{I}{y}}
          &= \exp\Bigl(\frac{\|\mu_0-y\|_2^2 - \|\mu_t-y\|_2^2}{2}\Bigr)
          \,,
          \label{eq:SS:LC:changeOfMeasure:ratio}
        \end{align} 
        By construction, 
        \[
        \mu_t = W_0^\top x + t\,V^\top x\,,
        \]
        and, conditioned on the event $\ensuremath{\mathscr{E}}$, 
        \[
        \snorm{V^\top x}_2 \le B^2\cdot O\sinparen{k^{3/2}}\,.
        \]
        Hence, we have
        \[
        \relax{\mu_t-y} \in \relax{\mu_0-y} \pm \relax{\mu_t-\mu_0} \in \relax{\mu_0-y} \pm t\,B^2\cdot O\sinparen{k^{3/2}}\,.
        \]
        Furthermore, under $\ensuremath{\mathscr{E}}$, 
        \[
        \relax{\mu_0}_2,~~~ \relax{y} ~~~\le~~~ B^2\cdot O\sinparen{k^{3/2}}\,.
        \]
        It follows that
        \[
        \relax{\mu_t-y}^2 \in \relax{\mu_0-y}^2 
        \pm 4t\,B^4\cdot O(k^3)
        \pm t^2\,B^4\cdot O(k^3)
        \overset{(t\le 1)}{\in} \relax{\mu_0-y}^2 \pm 5t\,B^4\cdot O(k^3)\,.
        \]
        Substituting this bound into \cref{eq:SS:LC:changeOfMeasure:ratio} gives
        \begin{align}
        \exp\inparen{-\frac{5t\,B^4}{2}\cdot O(k^3)}
        \le \frac{\normalMass{\mu_t}{I}{y}}{\normalMass{\mu_0}{I}{y}}
        \le \exp\inparen{\frac{5t\,B^4}{2}\cdot O(k^3)}\,.
        \label{eq:SS:LC:changeOfMeasure:Ratio2}
        \end{align} 
        Finally, for any function $f(y)$, using \cref{eq:SS:LC:changeOfMeasure:Ratio2} we obtain
        \begin{align*}
        \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\nolimits_t\insquare{f(y)}
          &= \frac{\int_{S(y_{\max})} f(y)\,\normalMass{\mu_t}{I}{y}\,{\rm d} y}{\normalMass{\mu_t}{I}{S(y_{\max})}}\\[1mm]
          &\in e^{5t\,B^4\cdot O(k^3)}\cdot \frac{\int_{S(y_{\max})} f(y)\,\normalMass{\mu_0}{I}{y}\,{\rm d} y}{\normalMass{\mu_0}{I}{S(y_{\max})}}\\
          &= e^{5t\,B^4\cdot O(k^3)}\cdot \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}\nolimits_0\insquare{f(y)}\,.
        \end{align*}
        This completes the change-of-measure argument.

\sloppy
        \Cref{part:SS:gradientOracle:unbiased} follows by definition.
        The formal proof of \Cref{part:SS:gradientOracle:secondMoment} is through an involved calculation
        and we defer it to \cref{sec:SS:secondMoment}.

        In order to see \Cref{part:SS:gradientOracle:algorithm},
        we note that it suffices to approximately sample \mbox{$z\sim \normal{W^\top x}{I}\mid z\in P(y_{\max})$}
        and output $\widetilde g(W) = xz^\top - xx^\top W$.
        We can express the event $z\in P(y_{\max})$ as union of events $\cup_{i\in [k]} P_i(y_{\max})$ where
        \[
            P_i(y_{\max}) \coloneqq \inbrace{z_i=y_{\max}\land z_j\leq y_{\max}, \forall j\neq i}.
        \]
        Now, given $z\in P(y_{\max})$,
        the conditional probability of $P_i(y_{\max})$ is given by
        \[
            \Pr\insquare{z\in P_i(y_{\max})\mid z\in P(y_{\max})}
            = \frac{\Pr[z_i=y_{\max}]\cdot \prod_{j\neq i} \Pr[z_j\leq y_{\max}]}{\sum_{i=1}^k \Pr[z_i=y_{\max}]\cdot \prod_{j\neq i} \Pr[z_j\leq y_{\max}]}.
        \]
        Furthermore,
        given $z\in P_i(y_{\max})$,
        we know that $z_i = y_{\max}$ and the rest of the coordinates $z_{-i}$ follows a truncated Gaussian distribution
        \[
            z_{-i}\mid z\in P_i(y_{\max}) \sim \normal{(W^\top x)_{-i}}{I}\mid z_{-i}\leq y_{\max}\,.
        \]
        
        The mixture probabilities can be expressed in closed form using the density and cumulative distribution function of the standard Gaussian distribution.
        We can thus estimate the mixture probabilities up to $\xi$-accuracy in $O(k\log\nfrac1\xi)$ time using an evaluation oracle for the error function (\emph{e.g.}{}, \cite[Proposition 3]{chevillard2012erf})
        and approximately sample from the mixture probability in $\xi$-TV distance.
        
        Suppose we sample $i$ from the mixture probabilities.
        We set $z_i = y_{\max}$ and sample the rest of the coordinates from the truncated Gaussian $z_{-i}\sim \normal{(W^\top x)_{-i}}{I}\mid z_{-i}\leq y_{\max}$.
        Since each coordinate of the truncated distribution is independent,
        we can perform the sampling for each coordinate individually.

        If $y_{\max}\geq w_j^\top x$,
        then we can simply perform rejection sampling with probability success at least $\nfrac12$.
        Suppose now that $y_{\max}< w_j^\top x$.
        \cite[Lemma 12]{daskalakis2019computationally} demonstrate how to approximately sample in $\xi$-TV distance from a truncated 1-dimensional Gaussian distribution $\truncatedNormal{\mu}{1}{[a, b]}$
        using inverse transform sampling.
        If $\alpha \coloneqq \normalMass{[a, b]}{\mu}{1}$,
        then their algorithm requires $\mathrm{poly}\log(\nfrac1\alpha, \nfrac1\xi)$ time.
        Fix a coordinate $z_j, j\neq i$.
        By \Cref{asmp:SS:separationBoundedness},
        $\relax{w_j}_2, \relax{{w^\star}_j}_2\leq C$.
        Since ${w^\star}_j^\top x\sim \normal{0}{{w^\star}_j^\top{w^\star}_j}$,
        $w_j\top x\sim \normal{0}{w_j^\top w_j}$,
        we see that $y_{\max} \geq -C-O(\sqrt{\log(\nfrac{1}{\delta})})$ and $w_j^\top x\leq C+O(\sqrt{\log(\nfrac{k}{\delta})})$ for all $j$
        with probability $1-\delta$ over the covariate $x$.
        In particular,
        $\abs{y_{\max} - w_j^\top x}\leq O(\sqrt{\log(\nfrac{k}{\delta})})$ with high probability
        so that by standard bounds on the Gaussian cumulative distribution function (\emph{e.g.}{}, \cite[Section 2.3]{kantor2015mathematics}),
        the survival probability $\alpha_j\coloneqq \normalMass{w_j^\top x}{1}{(-\infty, y_{\max}]}$
        is at least
        \[
            \Omega\inparen{\frac1{\sqrt{\log(\nfrac{k}{\delta})}} \exp\inparen{-\log(\nfrac{k}{\delta})}}
            = \Omega(\mathrm{poly}(\nfrac\delta{k}))\,.
        \]
        For any $a>0$,
        consider the event $z_j < y_{\max}-a \leq w_j^\top x - a$.
        We have
        \begin{align*}
            \Pr\insquare{z_j \leq y_{\max} - a\mid z_j\leq y_{\max}}
            = \frac{\Pr\insquare{z_j\leq y_{\max}-a}}{\Pr\insquare{z_j\leq y_{\max}}}
            \leq \frac1{\alpha_j} \Pr\insquare{z_j\leq w_j^\top x-a}
            \leq \mathrm{poly}(\nfrac{k}\delta) e^{-\frac{a^2}{2C^2}}\,.
        \end{align*}
        Choosing $a = \Omega(\log(\nfrac{k}{\delta\xi}))$ reduces the tail probability of the truncated Gaussian to at most $\xi$.
        We can thus run the inverse transform sampling algorithm of \cite{daskalakis2019computationally}
        on the distribution $\truncatedNormal{w_j^\top x}{1}{[y_{\max}-a, y_{\max}]}$ to approximately sample in $\xi$-TV distance from $\truncatedNormal{w_j^\top x}{1}{(-\infty, y_{\max}]}$.
        The running time is $\mathrm{poly}\log(\nfrac{k}\delta, \nfrac1\xi)$.

        Repeat this sampling algorithm for each coordinate $j\neq i$.
        Suppose we wish to bound the joint TV distance of every coordinate by $\xi$
        with probability $1-\delta$ over the observed covariate.
        This leads to a total running time of $k\cdot \mathrm{polylog}(\nfrac{k}\delta, \nfrac{k}\xi)$ for all sampling procedures.
        In the $\delta$ probability event of failure,
        we can simply output an arbitrary vector in $P(y_{\max})$, and the TV distance is at most $\xi+\delta$.

        Once we have the desired sample $z$,
        we can perform the matrix multiplications $x(z^\top - x^\top W)$ in the order given by the parenthesis in $O(kd)$ arithmetic operations.
        This yields the final running time guarantees.

nodes.statement: By Crefthm:SS:localConvexity, ensuremathL_hypoP is convex over K. Define \[ alpha coloneqq inparenfraccek^O(C^2/c^2) = poly(nfrac1k). \] Combining Crefthm:SS:localConvexity and Crefthm:info-pres-implies-strong-conv shows that ensuremathL_hypoP satisfies a Omega(alpha)-local growth condition (Crefdef:local-growth) over K. Creflem:SS:gradientOracle shows that we have an (approximate) stochastic gradient oracle with second moment G^2 = widetilde O(k^4d) and running time widetilde O(kd log(nfrac1delta)). Thus the given D-warm start has an objective value at most DG = O(sqrtdcdot poly(k)). As we would like an O(alpha^2varepsilon^2)-optimal solution in order to recover the parameters to accuracy varepsilon, Crefthm:SGD-local-growth-convergence ensures that it suffices to take \[ m = widetilde OinparenfracG^2alpha^4 varepsilon^2 = widetilde Oinparenfracdcdot poly(k)varepsilon^2 \] gradient steps with each step consuming one sample from the self-selection model. Each gradient computation takes widetilde O(kdlog(nfrac1varepsilon)) running time in order to reduce the joint TV-distance sampling error over all gradients to 0.01. Moreover, each gradient step requires O(kd) arithmetic operations. Thus the total running time becomes \[ widetilde O(mkd log(nfrac1varepsilon)) = widetilde Oinparenfracd^2cdot poly(k)varepsilon^2. \] Our algorithm recovers w_1^star, dots, w_k^star in varepsilon-Euclidean distance with probability 0.98 up to some permutation. As described in Crefsec:SGD:clusteringBoosting, we wish to repeat the algorithm O(log(nfrac1delta)) times and output the solution close to at least 50\% of the points. In our setting, we can interpret closeness under permutation as a metric over a quotient space over R^dtimes k and perform the clustering trick from Crefsec:SGD:clusteringBoosting using this metric.

By \Cref{thm:SS:localConvexity},
        $\ensuremath{\mathscr{L}}_{\hypo{P}}$ is convex over $K$.
        Define
        \[
            \alpha \coloneqq \inparen{\frac{c}{ek}}^{O(C^2/c^2)} = \mathrm{poly}(\nfrac1k).
        \]
        Combining \Cref{thm:SS:localConvexity} and \Cref{thm:info-pres-implies-strong-conv}
        shows that $\ensuremath{\mathscr{L}}_{\hypo{P}}$ satisfies a $\Omega(\alpha)$-local growth condition (\Cref{def:local-growth}) over $K$. 

        \Cref{lem:SS:gradientOracle} shows that
        we have an (approximate) stochastic gradient oracle
        with second moment $G^2 = \widetilde O(k^4d)$ and running time $\widetilde O(kd \log(\nfrac1\delta))$.
        Thus the given $D$-warm start has an objective value at most $DG = O(\sqrt{d}\cdot \mathrm{poly}(k))$.

        As we would like an $O(\alpha^2\varepsilon^2)$-optimal solution in order to recover the parameters to accuracy $\varepsilon$,
        \Cref{thm:SGD-local-growth-convergence} ensures that it suffices to take
        \[
            m = \widetilde O\inparen{\frac{G^2}{\alpha^4 \varepsilon^2}}
            = \widetilde O\inparen{\frac{d\cdot \mathrm{poly}(k)}{\varepsilon^2}}
        \]
        gradient steps with each step consuming one sample from the self-selection model.
        Each gradient computation takes $\widetilde O(kd\log(\nfrac1\varepsilon))$ running time 
        in order to reduce the joint TV-distance sampling error over all gradients to $0.01$.
        Moreover,
        each gradient step requires $O(kd)$ arithmetic operations.
        Thus the total running time becomes
        \[
            \widetilde O(mkd \log(\nfrac1\varepsilon))
            = \widetilde O\inparen{\frac{d^2\cdot \mathrm{poly}(k)}{\varepsilon^2}}.
        \] 
        Our algorithm recovers $w_1^\star, \dots, w_k^\star$ in $\varepsilon$-Euclidean distance with probability $0.98$ up to some permutation.
        As described in \Cref{sec:SGD:clusteringBoosting},
        we wish to repeat the algorithm $O(\log(\nfrac1\delta))$ times and output the solution close to at least 50\% of the points.
        In our setting,
        we can interpret closeness under permutation as a metric over a quotient space over $\mathbb{R}^{d\times k}$
        and perform the clustering trick from \Cref{sec:SGD:clusteringBoosting} using this metric.

nodes.raw_latex:
\label{lem:2ndPrice:LC:step1}
        For $\zeta\in(0,1)$ and $t=\zeta\cdot O\inparen{\frac{1}{B^4k^3}}$, 
        \begin{align*}
            \forall_{x\in \mathbb{R}^d}\,,~\forall_{y_{\max,2}\in \mathbb{R}}~\forall_{i_{\max}\in [k]}\,,\quad 
            \boldsymbol\NABLA^2 \ensuremath{\mathscr{L}}(W_t;x,y_{\max,2},i_{\max}) 
            &- \boldsymbol\NABLA^2 \ensuremath{\mathscr{L}}(W_0;x,y_{\max,2},i_{\max})\\
            &\qquad\succeq -\upgamma(x,y_{\max,2},i_{\max}) \cdot I_{k}\otimes xx^\top\,,
        \end{align*}
        where
        \[ 
            \upgamma(x,y_{\max,2},i_{\max}) \coloneqq 
                \Theta(k^2)
                \cdot
                \Bigl(\zeta + e^{-B^2 k/2}\Bigr)\cdot
                \Bigl(1 + y_{\max,2}^4 + \max\sinbrace{\|W_t^\top x\|_\infty, \|W_0^\top x\|_\infty}^4\Bigr)
                \,.
        \]

nodes.statement: One change required is in the proof of creflem:SS:LC:unconditionalMoments, which upper bounds \[ operatornamewithlimitsE_zsim normalW_t^top x1insquaresinanglev,z^2mid zin P(y_max) quadtextand operatornamewithlimitsE_zsim normalW_t^top x1insquaresinanglev,z^4mid zin P(y_max)\,. \] Its proof divides the moment into k-parts one corresponding to each coordinate of z and, further, breaks each conditioning zin P(y_max) into k-subparts corresponding to the k-parts of P_y_max; see creffig:self-selection-3D-distinct. One can repeat the same proof for P(y_max,2,i_max) since it has (k-1)-parts and these parts have a similar structure as the parts of P_y_max: they fix two coordinate's value and restrict the remaining (k-2)-coordinates to lie in an interval; see creffig:2nd-price-observation-distinct. One difference is that one of the slabs (which corresponds to i_max) pleases a constraint of the form z_igeq y_max,2 instead of z_ileq y_max,2, but this is easily handled by considering w=-z_i and using that operatornamewithlimitsE[w^2]=operatornamewithlimitsE[z^2] and operatornamewithlimitsE[w^4]=operatornamewithlimitsE[z^4].
nodes.raw_latex:
One change required is in the proof of \cref{lem:SS:LC:unconditionalMoments}, which upper bounds 
        \[
            \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}_{z\sim \normal{W_t^\top x}{1}}\insquare{\sinangle{v,z}^2\mid z\in P(y_{\max})}
            \quadtext{and}
            \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}_{z\sim \normal{W_t^\top x}{1}}\insquare{\sinangle{v,z}^4\mid z\in P(y_{\max})}\,.
        \]
        Its proof divides the moment into $k$-parts one corresponding to each coordinate of $z$ and, further, breaks each conditioning $z\in P(y_{\max})$ into $k$-subparts corresponding to the $k$-parts of $P_{y_{\max}}$; see \cref{fig:self-selection-3D-distinct}. 
        One can repeat the same proof for $P(y_{\max,2},i_{\max})$ since it has $(k-1)$-parts and these parts have a similar structure as the parts of $P_{y_{\max}}$: they fix two coordinate's value and restrict the remaining $(k-2)$-coordinates to lie in an interval; see \cref{fig:2nd-price-observation-distinct}. 
        One difference is that one of the slabs (which corresponds to $i_{\max}$) pleases a constraint of the form $z_i\geq y_{\max,2}$ instead of $z_i\leq y_{\max,2}$, but this is easily handled by considering $w=-z_i$ and using that $\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}[w^2]=\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}[z^2]$ and $\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}[w^4]=\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}[z^4]$.

nodes.statement: sloppy Crefpart:2ndPrice:gradientOracle:unbiased follows by definition. The formal proof of Crefpart:2ndPrice:gradientOracle:secondMoment is through an involved calculation and we defer it to crefsec:2ndPrice:secondMoment. The only necessary change from between Crefpart:SS:gradientOracle:algorithm in Creflem:SS:gradientOracle and Crefpart:2ndPrice:gradientOracle:algorithm is sampling from zsim normalW^top xImid zin P(y_max,2, i_max), which we now sketch. Decompose the set P(y_max,2, i_max) as cup_i_maxneq j [k] P_j(y_max,2, i_max) where \[ P_j(y_max,2, i_max) coloneqq inbrace z_i_maxgeq y_max,2,~~z_j=y_max,2~~and~~forall ellneq j, i_max, z_ellleq y_max,2 \,. \] Similar to Creflem:SS:gradientOracle, we can compute the probability zin P_j(y_max,2, i_max) given that zin P(y_max,2, i_max) by evaluating the density and cdf of the standard Gaussian distribution. Thus we can compute the conditional probability that z_j = y_max,2. Upon fixing the second max coordinate j, we sample the rest of the coordinates z_-j, -i_max independently using inverse transform sampling in an identical fashion to Creflem:SS:gradientOracle. Finally, we must sample z_i_maxsim truncatedNormalw_i_max^top x1[y_max,2, infty). This can also be done using inverse transform sampling.
nodes.raw_latex:
\sloppy
        \Cref{part:2ndPrice:gradientOracle:unbiased} follows by definition.
        The formal proof of \Cref{part:2ndPrice:gradientOracle:secondMoment} is through an involved calculation
        and we defer it to \cref{sec:2ndPrice:secondMoment}.
        The only necessary change from between \Cref{part:SS:gradientOracle:algorithm} in \Cref{lem:SS:gradientOracle} and \Cref{part:2ndPrice:gradientOracle:algorithm} is sampling from $z\sim \normal{W^\top x}{I}\mid z\in P(y_{\max,2}, i_{\max})$,
        which we now sketch.

        Decompose the set $P(y_{\max,2}, i_{\max})$ as
        $
            \cup_{i_{\max}\neq j [k]} P_{j}(y_{\max,2}, i_{\max})
        $
        where
        \[
            P_{j}(y_{\max,2}, i_{\max}) \coloneqq \inbrace{
                z_{i_{\max}}\geq y_{\max,2},~~z_j=y_{\max,2}~~\text{and}~~\forall \ell\neq j, i_{\max}, z_\ell\leq y_{\max,2}
            }\,.
        \]
        Similar to \Cref{lem:SS:gradientOracle},
        we can compute the probability $z\in P_j(y_{\max,2}, i_{\max})$ given that $z\in P(y_{\max,2}, i_{\max})$
        by evaluating the density and cdf of the standard Gaussian distribution.
        Thus we can compute the conditional probability that $z_j = y_{\max,2}$.
        Upon fixing the second max coordinate $j$,
        we sample the rest of the coordinates $z_{-j, -i_{\max}}$ independently using inverse transform sampling
        in an identical fashion to \Cref{lem:SS:gradientOracle}.
        Finally,
        we must sample $z_{i_{\max}}\sim \truncatedNormal{w_{i_{\max}}^\top x}{1}{[y_{\max,2}, \infty)}$.
        This can also be done using inverse transform sampling.

\label{thm:convexLocalPartitionMeanEstimation}
    Let $\varepsilon\in (0, 1]$.
    Suppose $\hypo{P}$ is a convex $R$-local $\alpha$-information preserving partition of $\mathbb{R}^d$ and $\relax{{\mu^\star}}_2\leq D$.
    There is an algorithm that outputs an estimate $\widetilde \mu$ satisfying
    \[
        \relax{\widetilde \mu - {\mu^\star}}_2 \leq \varepsilon
    \]
    with probability $1-\delta$. Moreover,
    the algorithm requires
    \[
        m = O\inparen{\frac{dR^2 + D^2}{\alpha^4 \varepsilon^2} \log^3\inparen{\frac{dRD}{\varepsilon \delta}}}
    \]
    samples from $\coarseNormal{{\mu^\star}}{I}{\hypo{P}}$ and $\mathrm{poly}(m, T_s)$ time,
    where $T_s$ is the time complexity of sampling from a Gaussian distribution truncated $P\cap B_\infty(0, R)$
    for some $P\in \hypo{P}$.

Consider a general $\alpha$-information preserving convex partition $\hypo{P}$ and $P\sim \coarseNormal{{\mu^\star}}{I}{\hypo{P}}$.
    Since $\relax{{\mu^\star}}_\infty\leq \relax{{\mu^\star}}_2\leq D$,
    setting $R = D + O(\log\nfrac{md}{\delta})$ means that any $m$-sample algorithm will not observe 
    a sample $P$ such that $P\cap B_\infty(0, R) = \varnothing$ with probability $1-\delta$.
    Define the partition $\hypo{P}(R)$ of $\mathbb{R}^d$ given by
    \[
        \hypo{P}(R)\coloneqq 
        \inbrace{P\cap B_\infty(0, R): P\in \hypo{P}, P\cap B_\infty(0, R)\neq \varnothing}
        \cup \inbrace{\set{x}\colon x\notin B_\infty(0, R)}\,.
    \]
    Since $\hypo{P}(R)$ is a refinement of $\hypo{P}$,
    it must also be $\alpha$-information preserving.
    Consider the set-valued algorithm $F\colon  \hypo{P}\to \hypo{P}(R)$ given  by
    \[
        P \mapsto 
        \begin{cases}
            P\cap B_\infty(0, R), &P\cap B_\infty(0, R)\neq \varnothing\,, \\
            \text{$\inbrace{x}$ for an arbitrary $x\in P$}, &P\cap B_\infty(0, R) = \varnothing\,.
        \end{cases}
    \]
    By the choice of $R$,
    with probability $1-\delta$,
    any $m$-sample algorithm will not distinguish between 
    samples from $\coarseNormal{{\mu^\star}}{I}{\hypo{P}(R)}$ and $F(P)$ for $P\sim \coarseNormal{{\mu^\star}}{I}{\hypo{P}}$.
    Moreover,
    we can sample from $P\cap B_\infty(0, R)$ as per \Cref{asmp:samplingOracle}.
    Thus we can simply run the algorithm from \Cref{thm:convexLocalPartitionMeanEstimation}
    with input samples $F(P)$ for $P\sim \coarseNormal{{\mu^\star}}{I}{\hypo{P}}$.

Define $\varepsilon_\ell \coloneqq 2^{-\ell} \varepsilon_0$.
    We will argue that $F(w^{(\ell)}) - F(w^\star) \leq \varepsilon_{\ell} + \varepsilon$

    We consider some $\ell\geq 1$.
    Remark that
    \[
        D_\ell = \frac{\varepsilon_{\ell-1}}{\eta \sqrt{\varepsilon}}
        \qquadtext{and}
        \upgamma_\ell = \frac{\varepsilon_\ell}{100G^2\tau}\,.

    we have

        \leq \frac{1}{\eta \sqrt\varepsilon} (F(w^{(\ell-1)}) - F(w^{(\ell-1)})_\varepsilon^\dagger)
        \leq \frac{\varepsilon_{\ell-1}}{\eta\sqrt\varepsilon}
        \leq D_\ell\,.

    \[

nodes.name: Boosting without Function Evaluation via Clustering
nodes.statement: In order to boost the probability of successfully recovering w^star, a standard trick is to repeat the algorithm O(log(nfrac1delta)) times and output the solution with smallest objective value. However, we do not have exact evaluation access to the log-likelihood functions we wish to optimize. demonstrate a ``clustering'' trick to avoid function evaluation. Suppose we repeat the algorithm in Crefthm:SGD-convergence O(log(nfrac1delta)) times. \label{sec:SGD:clusteringBoosting}
    In order to boost the probability of successfully recovering ${w^\star}$,
    a standard trick is to repeat the algorithm $O(\log(\nfrac1\delta))$ times and output the solution with smallest objective value.
    However,
    we do not have exact evaluation access to the log-likelihood functions we wish to optimize.
    \cite[Section 3.4.5]{daskalakis2018efficient} demonstrate a ``clustering'' trick to avoid function evaluation.
    Suppose we repeat the algorithm in \Cref{thm:SGD-convergence} $O(\log(\nfrac1\delta))$ times.
    A Chernoff bound yields that with high probability,
    at least $\nfrac23$ of the outputted points are $\varepsilon$-close to ${w^\star}$
    and thus are $2\varepsilon$-close to each other.
    Thus outputting any point which is at most $2\varepsilon$-close to at least 50\% of the points must be at most $3\varepsilon$-close to ${w^\star}$.

nodes.statement: Recall that, for some upgammain (0,nfrac12] and Rgeq 2, ensuremathE=ensuremathE_i,upgamma,R is the following event: \[ 1 ~leq~ fracinanglex, whw_i Rsqrtlognfrac1upgamma \,, ~ fracinanglex, whu 2sqrtlognfrac1upgamma ~leq~ 2\,. \] Here ucoloneqq v_i - inanglev_i,whw_iwhw_i is the component of v_i orthogonal to w_i and widehat u the unit vector parallel to u. In the special case, where v_i is parallel to w_i (and, hence, u=0), the definition of ensuremathE omits the bound on inanglex, whu. In this section, we prove that \[ Pr[ensuremathE] = upgamma^6+4R^2+logR\,. \] We will use the following standard facts. [E.g., Proposition 2.1.2 in citetvershynin2018high] The following tail bounds hold for all z>0 \[ frace^-z^2/2sqrt2uppiinparenfrac1z - frac1z^3 leq Pr_xsim customcalN(0,1)[xgeq z] leq frace^-z^2/2sqrt2uppifrac1z\,. \] We divide the proof into two parts. First, we prove the statement when v_i is not parallel to w_i. Then, we extend the proof to the special case where v_i is parallel to w_i. paragraphCase A (v_i is not parallel to w_i). Since whu is a projection of v_i in a space orthogonal to w_i, whu is orthogonal to w_i. Further since xsim customcalN(0,I) and wh w_i, wh u are orthonormal, sinanglex, whw_i and sinanglex, whu are independent random variables with distributions sinanglex, whw_isim customcalN(0,1) and sinanglex, whusim customcalN(0,1). Now, creffact:GaussianTail implies that Prinsquare frac sinanglex, whw_i Rsqrtlognfrac1upgamma > 2 &leq fracupgamma^4R^2sqrt2uppi cdot frac12Rsqrtlognfrac1upgamma\,,\\ Prinsquare frac sinanglex, whw_i Rsqrtlognfrac1upgamma geq 1 &geq fracupgamma^4R^2sqrt2uppi cdot frac1Rsqrtlognfrac1upgamma inparen 1 - frac1inparen Rsqrtlognfrac1upgamma ^2 ~~ StackrelRgeq 2\,,~upgammaleq nfrac12geq ~~ fracupgamma^4R^2sqrt2uppi cdot frac610Rsqrtlognfrac1upgamma \,. Hence, \[ Prinsquare fracsinanglex, whw_i Rsqrtlognfrac1upgamma in [1,2] geq fracupgamma^4R^2sqrt2uppi cdot frac110Rsqrtlognfrac1upgamma \,. addtocounterequation1tagtheequation \] Analogously, creffact:GaussianTail implies that \[ Prinsquare fracsinanglex, whu 2sqrtlognfrac1upgamma in [1,2] geq fracupgamma^16sqrt2uppi cdot frac120sqrtlognfrac1upgamma \,. addtocounterequation1tagtheequation \] Since sinanglex, whw_i and sinanglex, whu are independent random variables, it holds that \[ Pr[ensuremathE] = Prinsquare 1 ~leq~ fracinanglex, whw_i Rsqrtlognfrac1upgamma \,, ~ fracinanglex, whu 2sqrtlognfrac1upgamma ~leq~ 2 ~~ Stackrel textuptagform@\,,~ textuptagform@ geq ~~ fracupgamma^16+4R^22uppicdot frac1200Rlognfrac1upgamma\,. \] Since upgamma leq nfrac12, 2^11geq 400uppi, and zleq inparenlognfrac1z^-1 for any zin (0,1) it follows that \[ Pr[ensuremathE] geq upgamma^28+4R^2+logR ~~~Stackrel(Rgeq 1)geq~~~ upgamma^28+5R^2\,. \] paragraphCase B (v_i is parallel to w_i). In this case, ensuremathE is defined to be the following event \[ 1 ~leq~ fracinanglex, whw_i Rsqrtlognfrac1upgamma ~leq~ 2\,. \] Calculations from the previous case imply that \[ Pr[ensuremathE] geq fracupgamma^4R^2sqrt2uppicdot frac110Rsqrtlognfrac1upgamma\,. \] Since upgamma leq nfrac12, 2^5geq sqrt2uppicdot 10, and zleq inparensqrtlognfrac1z^-1 for any zin (0,1) it follows that \[ Pr[ensuremathE] geq upgamma^6+4R^2+logR ~~~Stackrel(Rgeq 1)geq~~~ upgamma^6(1+R^2)\,. \]

nodes.statement: Suppose v_i is not parallel to w_i; we handle the edge case where v_i is parallel to w_i separately. Let z_i be the component of v_i orthogonal to w_i. Recall that for each 1leq jleq k rho_j,V &= proj_span(v_i,w_i)(x)^top v_j = inanglex,whz_i sinanglev_j,whz_i + inanglex,whw_i sinanglev_j,whw_i\,,\\ rho_j,W &= proj_span(v_i,w_i)(x)^top w_j = inanglex,whz_i sinanglew_j,whz_i + inanglex,whw_i sinanglew_j,whw_i\,. We divide the proof into three parts corresponding to the three claims. paragraphProof of Claim 1. Observe that rho_i,W - rho_j,W &= inanglex,whw_isinanglew_i - w_j, whw_i + inanglex,whz_isinanglew_i - w_j, whz_i\,. First, we lower-bound the first term conditioned on ensuremathE, inanglex,whw_isinanglew_i - w_j, whw_i = inanglex,whw_i cdot fracrelaxw_i^2 - sinanglew_j,w_i relaxw_i_2 ~~~Stackrelcrefasmp:SS:separationBoundednessgeq ~~~ inanglex,whw_icdot c ~~ Stackrelrmcrefdef:SS:eventgeq ~~ cRsqrtlognfrac1upgamma\,. Next, we upper-bound the absolute value of the second term conditioned on ensuremathE, absinanglex,whz_isinanglew_i - w_j, whz_i leq absinanglex,whz_irelaxw_i - w_j ~~~Stackrelrmcrefasmp:SS:separationBoundednessleq ~~~ absinanglex,whz_icdot 2C ~~Stackrelrmcrefdef:SS:eventleq ~~ 8C cdot sqrtlognfrac1upgamma\,. nodes.raw_latex:
\citet{orjebin2014recursive} provide the following formulas for the second and fourth moments of the normal distribution truncated to $(-\infty,b]$:
            \begin{align*}
                \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}_{z\sim \normal{\mu}{1}}\insquare{z^2\mid z\leq b}
                    &= \mu^2 + 1 - \frac{(\mu+b)\,\phi(b-\mu)}{\Phi(b-\mu)}\,,
                    \addtocounter{equation}{1}\tag{\theequation}\label{eq:SS:LC:momentBound2}\\
                \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}_{z\sim \normal{\mu}{1}}\insquare{z^{\smash{4}}\mid z\leq b}
                    &=\mu^4 + 6\mu^2 + 3 - \frac{\bigl(b^3+b^2\mu+b\mu^2+3b+5\mu+\mu^3\bigr)\,\phi(b-\mu)}{\Phi(b-\mu)}\,.
                    \addtocounter{equation}{1}\tag{\theequation}\label{eq:SS:LC:momentBound4}
            \end{align*} 
            Where $\phi(\cdot)$ and $\Phi(\cdot)$ are the probability density function and the cumulative density function of the standard normal distribution.
            
             
            Since $\nfrac{\phi(z)}{\Phi(z)}\leq \abs{z}+1$ for $z\in \mathbb{R}$ (see \cref{fact:BoundOnMillsLikeRatio}),  \cref{eq:SS:LC:momentBound2} implies,
            \[
                \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}_{z\sim \normal{\mu}{1}}\insquare{z^{{2}}\mid z\leq b} 
                \le \mu^2+1 + \inparen{\abs{b}+\abs{\mu}}\,\inparen{1+\abs{b}+\abs{\mu}}
                \leq 2\inparen{1+\abs{b}+\abs{\mu}}^2 
                \,.
            \] 
            It remains to upper bound $\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}_{z\sim \normal{\mu}{1}}\insquare{z^{{4}}\mid z\leq b}$.
            To simplify the notation, define,
            \[
                M \coloneqq |b|+|\mu|\,.
            \]
            Since $\left|b^3+b^2\mu+b\mu^2+\mu^3\right|\le M^3$, $|3b+5\mu|\le 5M$, and $\nfrac{\phi(z)}{\Phi(z)}\leq \abs{z}+1$ for $z\in \mathbb{R}$ (see \cref{fact:BoundOnMillsLikeRatio}),  \cref{eq:SS:LC:momentBound4} implies,
            \[
                \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}_{z\sim \normal{\mu}{1}}\insquare{z^{{4}}\mid z\leq b}
                \le 
                    \mu^4+6\mu^2+3 
                    +
                    \inparen{
                        M^3
                        +
                        5 M
                    } 
                    \inparen{1 + M}
                \,.
            \]
            Using $\mu^4+6\mu^2+3 \leq M^4 + 9 M^2$ and $(z^3+5z)(z+1) = z^4 + z^3 + 5z^2 + 5z$ implies 
            \[
                \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}_{z\sim \normal{\mu}{1}}\insquare{z^{{4}}\mid z\leq b}
                \leq 
                M^4 + 9M^2 + (M^3+5M)(M+1)
                \leq 2M^4 + M^3 + 14M^2 + 5M\,.
            \]
            This implies the result since $M\geq 0$, $2z^4 + z^3 + 14z^2 + 5z\leq 3\inparen{1+z}^4$ for any $z\geq 0$.

We divide the proof into two cases.
            \begin{itemize}
                \item \textbf{Case A ($z\geq 0$):}~~
                    Since \(\Phi(z)\ge \Phi(0)=\nfrac{1}{2}\) for \(z\ge 0\), $\nfrac{\phi(z)}{\Phi(z)} \le 2\phi(z)$.
                    Further, $\phi(z)=\inparen{\nfrac{1}{\sqrt{2\uppi}}}e^{-z^2/2}$ is maximized at \(z=0\), so that for \(z\ge 0\), $2\phi(z) \le 2\phi(0)=\sqrt{\sfrac{2}{\uppi}} \le 0.8\,.$
                    But we also have \(|z|+1=z+1\ge 1\) and, hence, $\nfrac{\phi(z)}{\Phi(z)} \le 0.8 \le z+1 = |z|+1$.
                \item \textbf{Case B ($z < 0$):}~~
                    Set \(w=-z>0\). By the symmetry of the standard normal density, we have
                    \[
                        \frac{\phi(z)}{\Phi(z)} = \frac{\phi(-w)}{\Phi(-w)} = \frac{\phi(w)}{1-\Phi(w)}\,.
                    \]
                    Define the function
                    \[
                        g(w) = (w+1)(1-\Phi(w)) - \phi(w)\,,\quad w>0\,.
                    \]
                    We claim that \(g(w)\ge 0\) for all \(w>0\): this holds because of the standard lower bound $1-\Phi(x)\geq \phi(x) \cdot \frac{2}{\sqrt{4+x^2}+x}$ for $x\geq 0$ (see  Equation (3) in \citet{duembgen2010boundingstandardgaussiantail}) and the fact that $z+1\geq \frac{1}{2}\sinparen{\sqrt{4+z^2}+z}$ for $z\geq 0$.
                    Thus, we conclude $(w+1)(1-\Phi(w)) \ge \phi(w)$ or equivalently,
                    \[
                    \frac{\phi(w)}{1-\Phi(w)} \le w+1\,.
                    \]
                    Returning to the variable \(z\) (with \(w=-z\)), we deduce
                    \[
                    \frac{\phi(z)}{\Phi(z)} \le |z| + 1\,.
                    \]
            \end{itemize}

nodes.name: Facet-Complexity
nodes.statement: We say that a polytope Psubseteq R^d has facet-complexity at most varphi_P if there exists a system of inequalities with rational coefficients that has solution set P and such that the bit-encoding length of each inequality of the system is at most varphi_P. In case P=R^d, we require varphi_Pgeq d+1.

We say that a polytope $P\subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ has \emph{facet-complexity} at most $\varphi_P$
        if there exists a system of inequalities with rational coefficients that has solution set $P$ and such that the bit-encoding length of each inequality of the system is at most $\varphi_P$.
        In case $P=\mathbb{R}^d$,
        we require $\varphi_P\geq d+1$.
